notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23, head d04061d, uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call (tool calls are only Read on the input file, Write, Edit and Bash), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires; skills_listed is 209. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since ba24972 (git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/): in SKILL.md, "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" gained paragraphs on patterns versus dot access and on nested chains, and "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" was rewritten; in ex_unit.md, "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" gained a sentence on crash reports. None of the eight graded rules changed, so all eight are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/test-writing-*.json. The caller's note about one bullet per sentence for the rewritten rules refers to webhook-parser.md and library-client.md; test-writing.md has no such bullets and neither rewritten rule is in its list. Neither rewritten rule is broken in any file here: no test body pulls a single field out of a held value with a pattern, and no file has a multi-clause function binding fields in its heads (the test heads %{server: server} are single-clause). No run uses capture_log for crash reports.

Rule counts (runs violating, of 5): "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" 5 (opus-1 and haiku-1 register the test process, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 use the application env, sonnet-2 uses :persistent_term), from 4 in 2026-10-22-d (opus-1 was clean there through $ancestors). "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" 4 (opus-1 clean), as 4 in 2026-10-22-d. "Assert with patterns" 4 (haiku-1 clean), from 3. "Wait for messages, not for time" 5, as 5. "Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" 4 (haiku-2 clean), as 4. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" 0. "Use setup for shared data" 0, from 1. "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" 0.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (unchanged). Describe blocks joining subscribe/3 and subscribers/2: haiku-1 line 40, haiku-2 line 36, sonnet-1 line 66. Test names violating the test-name sentence: haiku-1 line 41 "subscribe/3 returns :ok" and line 77 "publish/3 returns :ok"; sonnet-1 line 67 "returns :ok" and line 100 "works through the registered name"; sonnet-2 line 83 "returns :ok for a pid and for an email address". (haiku-1 line 108, sonnet-2 line 152), "publishing to a topic with no subscribers is a no-op" (sonnet-1 line 145), "is empty for an unknown topic" (sonnet-2 line 90), "the server keeps running" (sonnet-2 line 241) and "keeps running when the mailer returns an error" (sonnet-2 line 168), which name an effect.

"Assert with patterns" (unchanged), bare matches counted as in 2026-10-22-c/-d (a literal, tuple, list or map on the left, without assert, inside a test block; not plain-variable bindings or matches in helpers): opus-1 25, all :ok = calls (lines 40, 51, 52, 53, 62, 69, 70, 72, 79, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94, 104, 105, 115, 116, 117, 128, 129, 140, 141, 153, 156); haiku-1 0; haiku-2 21 (lines 38, 44, 50, 51, 58, 71, 79, 81, 87, 89, 95, 103, 105, 111, 112, 114, 124, 125, 135, 136, 144); sonnet-1 1 (line 54: {:ok, pid} = Subscriptions.start_link(mailer: TestMailer)); sonnet-2 0. sonnet-2 is violated by line 71: assert is_pid(Process.whereis(server)), the construct 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 graded violated; sonnet-1 line 133: assert length(pids) == 3 is listed as 2026-10-22 listed it. No run uses elem/2, puts the expected value on the left of ==, or binds a held value and compares it with == afterwards (opus-1 line 151 and sonnet-2 line 249 compare a whereis result with a held pid, value under test on the left).

"Wait for messages, not for time" (unchanged). Process.sleep polling after exits in all five: opus-1 line 181, haiku-1 line 286, haiku-2 line 177, sonnet-1 line 47, sonnet-2 line 64. :DOWN patterns: opus-1 none; haiku-1 line 271 _ (helper exit_process/2); haiku-2 line 167 _reason (helper stop_and_wait/1); sonnet-1 lines 211 and 265 _; sonnet-2 none. opus-1 and sonnet-2 never monitor the exiting subscriber. Single assert Process.alive? checks (haiku-1 line 168, sonnet-1 lines 249, 259, sonnet-2 line 250) are not polling and are not counted.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged). start_link from a test: haiku-1 line 178 and sonnet-2 lines 77-78 (missing-mailer failure), sonnet-1 lines 54 (default-name test) and 62 (missing-mailer failure). opus-1 line 24 starts every test's server under the default global name with only one test (line 150) about that default, graded violated as 2026-10-22-b and -c graded the same shape. sonnet-1 line 28 gives every test the fixed name :subscriptions_under_test, graded violated as 2026-10-22 graded its sonnet-1. haiku-2 is clean: unique names (line 29) and the default name only in its tagged default-name test (line 69), inside an async: false module, which earlier grades do not count.

"Use setup for shared data", "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" (unchanged) are clean in 5 of 5: every setup returns a map matched in test heads (haiku-2 returns :ok only in the branch for its tagged default-name test); every double is a module with @behaviour Notify.Mailer passed as :mailer; no test module has a @moduledoc, and the directives open each body (use / import / alias in haiku-1, use / alias in the others).

Outside the list: haiku-1 (lines 282-283) and sonnet-1 (line 28) fail mix format --check-formatted, recorded under "Before you finish". Test support modules without @moduledoc (sonnet-1 TestMailer, sonnet-2 Mailer and FailingMailer), private helpers above the tests (sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and comments on private helpers are not counted, as in earlier grades. No single-step pipes, captures, multi-line inline arguments in unbound calls, or wrapped do: bodies in any file.
